newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 18.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Up to 80,000 businesses may be affected by the import deposit plan approved on Wednesday. From Monday, April 21, every importer will have to place in one of five chosen banks a deposit of 20 percent of the price of the imported food and consumer goods -- including cars -- for 180 days.

- Ceska Energetika obtained a new, and possibly completely independent central energy control (UED), which will be strategic for the operation of energy systems and will ensure a sufficient source of energy.

- Deutsch Bank applied for the tender for the sale of the state's one-third stake in bank IPB. The director of IPB says there are now 14 potential investors in the tender, including ABN AMRO, ING and Nomura.
- Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec and Lithuanian Parliamentary Chairman Vytautas Lansbergis met yesterday in Prague and discussed the attempts of the two countries to enter the EU and NATO.

LIDOVE NOVINY - The new import deposit will be collected beginning Monday by five domestic commercial banks - Komercni Banka, IPB, Ceska Sporitelna, CSOB and Union Bankia. The deposit will affect imports of passenger cars, "means of transport", motorcycles, bicycles, tires, textile products, minaral oils, explosives, tobacco, drinks, meat and sugar.
- As of yesterday, the new owner of the majority stake in Poldi Steel is Blax Corporation from Lichtenstein. Blax bought it for four billion crowns from Pro Win.

- Transport and Communication Minister Martin Riman spoke with the chairman of the engineers' federation, Frantisek Pospisil, yesterday and met with the chairman of the railway workers' union, Jaromir Dusek, about renewing talks on the collective contract at Czech Railways. MLADA FRONTA DNES - The first reaction from individual companies and state institutions to the cabinet's campaign against high increases in wages is that the pressure will not significantly slow down the wage growth, but will cause a wave of lay-offs.

- Velkomoravska Banka, which is currently under compulsory administration, is suing Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB) over shares worth about 200 million crowns which the two banks exchanges between themselves at the end of 1995.

PRAVO - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who will arrive in Prague on Sunday for a two day visit, confirmed that Russia will not place any sanctions against the Czech Republic in connection with its entry into NATO.
- American State Street Bank recently succeeded in obtaining a 10 percent stake in CKD holding, which has most likely been behind the dramatic increase in CKD's share price.

- The cabinet's economic measures will ease the trade deficit, which is estimated at 220 billion crowns this year, by between 30 and 50 billion crowns, according to Vladimir Kreidl from Patria Finance. He added that there will be slower growth in GDP.
